svg.title: Transport processes
svg.desc: Diffusion: Net movement: gas/dissolved particles, high → low concentration, down the gradient. Random movement; no respiration energy. Examples: O₂, CO₂; urea from cells into blood plasma. At equilibrium particles move, but no net movement. Faster diffusion: Steeper gradient: greater net movement/second. Hotter: more kinetic energy. Larger area: more particles cross. Thinner barrier: shorter diffusion path. Osmosis: Water: dilute → concentrated solution through a partially permeable membrane. Dilute side has more water relative to solute. Water crosses; some solutes cannot. No respiration energy. Movement is both ways; arrows show the net direction. Water gain or loss: Dilute outside → water enters. Plant: vacuole fills, turgid; wall prevents bursting. Animal: may swell/burst. Concentrated outside → water leaves. Plant: flaccid; severe loss → plasmolysis (membrane pulls from wall). Animal: shrinks. Active transport: Substances move low → high, against the gradient, via membrane proteins. Needs energy from respiration, like moving uphill. Diffusion/osmosis move down gradients; only osmosis is water-only. Where it helps: Roots: take up minerals for growth even when soil concentration is lower. Gut: absorbs sugars into blood even when blood concentration is higher; sugars fuel respiration. Many mitochondria support high energy demand. Osmosis practical: Vary salt/sugar concentration; use equal-size potato cylinders. Weigh initially; equal solution volumes, including distilled water. Control tissue source, size, time and temperature. Blot consistently, reweigh; repeat and calculate means. Blotting removes surface liquid; cut safely. Calculate & interpret: % change = (final − initial) ÷ initial × 100. 2.50 → 2.20 g: −0.30 ÷ 2.50 × 100 = −12%. Gain +; loss −. Plot concentration (x), mean % change (y). Best-fit curve’s 0% crossing = no net movement, not no movement. Rate = change ÷ time: 0.12 g ÷ 30 min = 0.004 g/min. Check anomalies; repeat/test nearer zero.
